name: memcore-memory
author: Kovács-Dobos Ádám
description: Local-first encrypted memory for AI agents: AES-256-GCM SQLite store, 4-tier Ebbinghaus forgetting, hybrid retrieval (vector, BM25, graph and metadata arms re-ranked by recency and importance priors, weighted RRF), encrypted knowledge graph

env.MNEM_DATA_DIR: Data directory (defaults to ~/.memcore). Local mode only.
env.MNEM_MASTER_PASSWORD: Required when the master key is password-protected; stdio has no terminal to prompt on. Local mode only.
env.MNEM_REMOTE_URL: Equivalent to --remote: proxy to a running REST instance instead of opening a local store. An exported value switches `server mcp` to bridge mode; the mode is printed to stderr at startup
env.MNEM_API_KEY: Bridge mode only (also --api-key): sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' to a --remote instance that sets MNEM_API_KEY

remote_mode.note: Forwards every tool to POST /mcp/call on a running instance, which dispatches through the same HANDLERS table as the stdio server - so the tool surface cannot drift between the two. Required whenever the real store lives inside a container: a host-side process opening its own data dir is a different database, not the same memory. memory_export/memory_import take a file name inside <data_dir>/exports on the server (/data/exports in the container).

notes.tool_count: Was previously listed as 33. Four names (sync_add_peer, sync_broadcast, sync_merge, config_set) were removed rather than kept as no-ops: they need a live P2P node or a writable config store that the stdio process does not have. Every tool listed here is backed by a real implementation - see the import-time check in mcp/server.py.
notes.protocol_version: Not pinned here: the MCP SDK (mcp>=2.2) negotiates the protocol version at runtime. A hard-coded mcp_version field went stale and was removed on 2026-09-25.
notes.not_implemented: sync_status and sync_peers report configuration only: P2P sync is not implemented. The PII filter, audit log and reranker are not wired into any request path; config_get lists them under not_implemented.
